conflicts.subject: file
conflicts.detail: File primary keys differ (A: text, B: unknown)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: One File table keyed by id TEXT holding a uuid4 hex. B never persisted files (it receives a dict) and A's store is not in the source, so there are no existing rows to re-key; no legacy_id needed.

conflicts.subject: owner
conflicts.detail: No source authenticates anyone: A takes owner_id from the caller and C has no identity at all, yet the merged app must know who owns a file
solutions: Minimal accounts: username + password (salted PBKDF2), opaque session token in an http-only cookie
Trust an owner id header (unsafe)
conflicts.recommended: Minimal accounts with a salted PBKDF2 password and a server-side session in an http-only cookie (standard library only)

resolution.decision: Minimal accounts: register/login with username + password hashed by salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256; server-side session token (secrets.token_urlsafe) in an http-only SameSite=Strict cookie.

conflicts.subject: file-access
conflicts.detail: A scopes every file action by owner_id; C has no owner concept, so any caller could create or revoke a link for any file_id
solutions: Owner-only link create/revoke; a token grants read-only access to that one file
Let anyone with the file id share it (weakens A's owner scoping)
conflicts.recommended: Owner-only link create/revoke; a valid token (and password, if set) grants read-only metadata, preview and download of that one file

resolution.decision: Owner-only link create/revoke and owner-only file list/delete/preview/content; a valid unexpired token (plus password if set) grants read-only metadata, preview and download of that one file.

conflicts.subject: link-password-hash
conflicts.detail: C stores link passwords as unsalted SHA-256 and compares with !=; the unified app's rule is a slow salted hash and constant-time compare
solutions: Salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with hmac.compare_digest
Keep C's unsalted SHA-256

resolution.decision: Salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with hmac.compare_digest for link passwords.

conflicts.subject: file.id
conflicts.detail: File.id types differ (A: text, B: str)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: id is TEXT in SQLite and str in Python; A's text and B's str are the same value type.

conflicts.subject: file.name
conflicts.detail: File.name types differ (A: text, B: str)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: name is TEXT in SQLite and str in Python; no conversion needed.

conflicts.subject: thumbnail-url
conflicts.detail: B returns /thumbs/<id>.png but nothing creates or serves it, and resizing needs an imaging library the standard library lacks
solutions: Preview URL points at a route that serves the original image (owner route or link route)
Defer image preview
conflicts.recommended: Serve the original image with its content type at /api/files/<id>/content (owner) or /s/<token>/content (link)

resolution.decision: Image preview URL points at /api/files/<id>/content (owner) or /s/<token>/content (link); no resizing.

conflicts.subject: file
conflicts.detail: File exists in A:File, B:File; fields not shared: created_at (only A), data (only B), owner_id (only A), size (only A)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge into one entity; list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge into one File entity with A's fields (id, owner_id, name, size, created_at); B's data field lives in file_content (see database:storage:file-bytes).

conflicts.subject: file-delete-links
conflicts.detail: Deleting a file in A would leave C's links pointing at a missing file_id
solutions: Delete a file's share links with it (foreign key ON DELETE CASCADE)
Keep links and return 404 when opened
conflicts.recommended: ON DELETE CASCADE from share_links.file_id to files.id

resolution.decision: share_links.file_id REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE CASCADE (foreign keys enabled per connection).

conflicts.subject: file-bytes
conflicts.detail: A's files table has no column for the file's bytes, but B's preview needs them
solutions: Store bytes in a separate SQLite BLOB table keyed by file id (max 10 MB each)
Store bytes on disk under a data folder
conflicts.recommended: Separate file_content table (file_id primary key, data BLOB) so listing never loads bytes

resolution.decision: file_content(file_id PK REFERENCES files ON DELETE CASCADE, data BLOB).
